### Introduction to Shiny Apps

- When we want to make R code accessible outside of an R or RStudio environment, for example:
  - Teaching a package
  - Showing data visualizations to non-experts
  - Streamlining certain code-intensive things (like database queries or visualizing bulky simulation outputs)
- Examples:
  - Teaching populations growth models [Populations Dynamics Lab](https://nsilbiger.shinyapps.io/PopulationDynamicsLab/)
  - Visualize model predictions [Marine Mammal Bycatch model](https://msiple.shinyapps.io/mmrefpoints/)

```{r Load Packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(peRReo)
library(shiny)
```

## Starting a New Shiny App

- Needs to be in its own folder, and usually best for it to be its own standalone repository
- For today, its folder is within `Gonzalez-Zamora`
  - `GonzalezZamora_Shiny`

Two Components of Shiny Apps

1.  The `ui` (user interface) object dictates the appearance of the app. The UI functions to write HTML
2.  The `server()` functions contains rendering expressions that create the objects to display

- The server functions and UI object are passed to the `shinyApp()` function to create a Shiny app object
  - When saving the script in your app, create a folder with the name of your app and then save the script as app.R.
  - You MUST save the script with this name for it to work.
  - Also, all files associated with your app must be in this folder.

```{r App Template}
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage('Hello World')

server <- function(input, output){}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

## Add Elements to App Using `fluidPage()`

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
ui <- fluidPage(
  # Inputs functions
  # Outputs functions
)
```

## Create an Input Function

- There are many types of inputs
- Syntax for all is *`type`*`Input`
  - To make a slider: `sliderInput()`

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
            label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
            value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
            )

# BEHIND THE SCENES
<div class="form-group shiny-input-container">
<label class="control-label" for="num">Choose a number</label>
<input class="js-range-slider" id="num" data-min="1" data-max="100"
data-from="25" data-step="1" data-grid="true" data-grid-num="9.9"
data-grid-snap="false" data-prettify-separator="," data-keyboard="true"
data-keyboard-step="1.01010101010101"/>
</div>
```

## Shiny Widget Options for Inputs

[Shiny Widgets with Code](https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/widget-gallery.html) [Shiny Widgets Package](https://dreamrs.github.io/shinyWidgets/)

## Syntax

`sliderInput(inputId = "num", label = 'Choose a number", ...)`

- `sliderInput()`
- `inputeId` = input name for internal use
- `label` = label to display
- `...` = input specific arguments
- `?sliderInput`

### Outputs

- `dataTableOutput()` = an interactive table

- `htmlOutput()` = raw HTML

- `imageOutput()` = image

- `plotOutput()` = plot

- `tableOutput()` = table

- `textOutput()` = text

- `uiOutput()` = a Shiny UI element

- `verbatimTextOutput()` = text

- To display an outputt add it to `fluidPage()` with an `Output()` function

`plotOutput`("hist")\`

- `plotOutput()` = type of output to display
- `("hist")` = name to give to the output object

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
            label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
            value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
            ),
  plotOutput("hist") # creates space for a plot called hist
)

server <- function(input, output){}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

# Code creates the space for a new plot, but nothing happens yet
```

### The Server

- 3 rules to write the server function:

1.  Save Objects to Display to `output$`
2.  Build Objects to Display with `render*({})`
3.  Access the input Values with `input$`

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# 1.
server <- function(input, output){
  output$hist <- # code
}

# Look back to the ui, hist is spelled identically to the name in the plotOutput() function

# 2.
server <- function(input, output){
  output$hist <- renderPlot({

    # R code to make the hist output goes here
  })
}

# 3.
library(tidyverse)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
            label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
            value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
            ),
  plotOutput("hist") # creates space for a plot called hist
)

server <- function(input, output){

   output$hist <- renderPlot({

     # {} allows us to put all our R code in one nice chunk
    data <- tibble(x = rnorm(input$num)) # number of points set by the slider

    ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) + # make a histogram
      geom_histogram()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

Replaced `100` with `input$num`. Notice that `num` comes from what we put in our `inputId`, exact same spelling.

## Types of Renders

- `renderDataTable()` = interactive table
- `renderImage()` = an image
- `renderPlot()` = a plot
- `renderPrint()` = a code block of printed output
- `renderTable()` = a table
- `renderText()` = a character string
- `renderUI()` = a Shiny UI element

## Modifying Inputs

- Let’s say we want to write an input where the user can create whatever title they want by typing it into a box.
  - Let’s update our ui to have a `textInput()`
- Let’s say we want to add a data table below the histogram that has all the summary statistics.
  - We need to add another ui element that creates a place to put the table.
  - We will use `verbatimTextOutput()`

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# Modify using textInput()

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
            label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
            value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
            ),
  textInput(inputId = "title", # new Id is title
          label = "Write a title",
          value = "Histogram of Random Normal Values"), # starting title
  plotOutput("hist") # creates space for a plot called hist
)

# Modify using verbatimTextOutput()
ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
            label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
            value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
            ),
  textInput(inputId = "title", # new Id is title
          label = "Write a title",
          value = "Histogram of Random Normal Values"), # starting title
  plotOutput("hist"), # creates space for a plot called hist
  verbatimTextOutput("stats") # create a space for stats
)

# Calculate the Summary Stats with renderprint()

server <- function(input, output){

   output$hist <- renderPlot({

     # {} allows us to put all our R code in one nice chunk
    data <- tibble(x = rnorm(input$num)) # number of points set by the slider

    ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) + # make a histogram
      geom_histogram() +
      labs(title = input$title) # add a new title
  })

   output$stats <- renderPrint({
     summary(rnorm(input$num)) # calculate summary stats based on the numbers
   })
}
```

### Cleaning Code

- Here, we used `input$num` twice: once in the plot and once in the summary stats.
- This actually created two separate random distributions and the stats actually are not directly related to the plots.
- We need to build a *reactive* object so the same dataframe is being used throughout all the code.
- We can use `reactive()` to build a reactive object (reactive expression)

## Reactive Objects

- Call reactive object like a function

- Reactive expressions cache their values, app runs much faster

- But aware:

  - A reactive object must be called like a function.
  - `ggplot(data, ...)` on line 23 is wrong — the plot needs `ggplot(data(), ...)`
  - Forgetting the parentheses is one of the most common Shiny errors `(“object of type ‘closure’ is not subsettable”)`

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num", # ID name for the input
              label = "Choose a number", # Label above the input
              value = 25, min = 1, max = 100 # values for the slider
  ),
  textInput(inputId = "title", # new Id is title
            label = "Write a title",
            value = "Histogram of Random Normal Values"), # starting title
  plotOutput("hist"), # creates space for a plot called hist
  verbatimTextOutput("stats") # create a space for stats
)

server <- function(input, output){

  data <- reactive({
     tibble(x = rnorm(input$num)) # number of points set by the slider
  })

  output$hist <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) + # make a histogram
      geom_histogram() +
      labs(title = input$title) # add a new title
  })
  output$stats <- renderPrint({
    summary(rnorm(input$num)) # calculate summary stats based on the numbers
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Building Stars App

```{r}
stars <- read_csv("../Data/stars.csv")

glimpse(stars)
```

## Add `selectInput` to Set Minimum Count

- `selectInput(inputId, label, choices)` creates a dropdown menu. We’ll use it to pick a minimum count of sea stars

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(inputId = "min_stars", # ID name for the input
              label = "Show sites with at least this many sea stars:",
              choices = c(1, 5, 10, 20), # threshold options
              selected = 5 # the threshold that shows first
              ),
  plotOutput("star_map") # creates space for the map
)

server <- function(input, output){}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

## Filter the Data in the Server

- Use `filter()` inside a reactive to keep only the sites that meet the threshold.
  - Each point is a site, sized by the number of sea stars counted there

```{r}
server <- function(input, output){

  kept_sites <- reactive({
    stars |>
      # selectInput returns choices as STRINGS, so convert back to numeric!
      filter(star_no >= as.numeric(input$min_stars)) # sites above threshold
  })

  output$star_map <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(kept_sites(), aes(x = long, y = lat)) +
      geom_point(aes(size = star_no), color = "red") + # points sized by count
      labs(size = "Sea stars counted")
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

The `filter()` lives inside `reactive()`, so the map re-filters every time the user picks a new threshold — and both the reactive pattern and the `*Input/*Output` naming rules are exactly what we just learned with the histogram app.

### Publishing Shiny App to Posit Connect

1.  Run your app locally (source `app.R`) so it’s live in the Viewer pane.
2.  Click blue Publish button in the Viewer pane
3.  In the publishing dialog, choose Posit Connect Cloud as the destination and your account.
4.  Confirm the files being bundled (make sure `app.R` and any data files are included), then click Publish
5.  Watch the deployment progress in the Jobs pane, then open the link to your live app.

- To update your app after changes, just click Publish again — it redeploys to the same content on Connect
- You can also deploy from the console with `rsconnect::deployApp()`

### Layout & Theming with `{bslib}`

- `{bslib}` is the modern way to build app layouts and themes
- Replaces the older `shinythemes` and `shinydashboard` packages and works with Bootstrap 5
- [bslib documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/)
- [Bootswatch themes](https://bootswatch.com/)

```{r}
library(bslib)


ui <- page_sidebar(
  theme = bs_theme(bootswatch = "cerulean"), # pick a Bootswatch theme
  sidebar = sidebar(                        # everything in the sidebar
    sliderInput(inputId = "num",
                label = "Choose a number",
                value = 25, min = 1, max = 100),
    textInput(inputId = "title",
              label = "Write a title",
              value = "Histogram of Random Normal Values")
  ),
  card(                                     # main content in cards
    card_header("Histogram"),
    plotOutput("hist")
  ),
  card(
    card_header("Summary statistics"),
    verbatimTextOutput("stats")
  )
)
```
